LESSON: RHYTHM AND PATTERN MAKING

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS
Strand: Creating and Executing
Topic 1.4: Rhythm and Pattern Making

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Rhythm and Pattern Making. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: Why create rhythm in different beat patterns?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. compose a rhythm using a combination of musical notes and their rests

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

• Today’s maths focus is Rhythm and Pattern Making.

• Start with objects you can touch or draw — stones, sticks, bottle tops, or drawings in your book.

• Say the steps aloud as you work so you do not skip a stage.

• Check your answer with a second method or by estimating.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: At the market, count 10 mangoes and put them in 2 groups of 5.

Example 2: In class, count the desks in your row and write the number in figures and in words.

Example 3: If you have 7 shillings and receive 5 more, you have 12 shillings.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Solve three short problems about Rhythm and Pattern Making using drawings.
2. Explain one solution to a partner in your own words.
3. Make up one new word problem set in your county or school.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five practice questions and solve them in your book.
2. Show your working clearly — not only the final answer.
3. Teach a younger learner one idea from this lesson with bottle tops or drawings.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Listen to /sing familiar songs and identify words with the French rhythm names taa, ta-te, taa-aa, taa-aa-aa, taa-aa-aa-aa,
2. Tap/ clap/stamp and recite rhythmic patterns using French rhythm names,
3. Apply composition techniques to compose original rhythmic patterns using French rhythm names or note symbols, and their rests,
4. Listen to songs and identify songs in three -beat patterns, Why create rhythm in different beat patterns? 9 f) value rhythmic patterns created by self and others.
5. Sing and conduct/beat time of songs in three -beat patterns,

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Use objects or drawings when a sum feels hard.
2. Check every answer.
3. Rhythm and Pattern Making is used in real Kenyan life — market, school, and home.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
